- Green shifters probably shift rows to the right

- Row 35: 10 blocks (bottom horizontal row)

- Top cap (row 17): 5 blocks
- Bottom cap (row 44): 5 blocks
The shifters are at:
- Red: (16,19), (25,13), (34,13)
- Green: (16,38), (25,47), (34,47)
The y-coordinates 16, 25, 34 correspond to:
- 16: near the top cap (row 17)
- 25: near the top row (row 26)
- 34: near the bottom row (row 35)
So:
- Shifter pair at y=16 controls the top cap (row 17)
- Shifter pair at y=25 controls the top row (row 26)
- Shifter pair at y=34 controls the bottom row (row 35)
Wait, but there are also left and right columns. Maybe the shifters control different parts:
- Red shifters on the left control left-to-right shifts
- Green shifters on the right control right-to-left shifts

- Green shifters shift CW (right for horizontal, down for vertical)

nodes = seg['nodes']

frame_blocks = []
for n in nodes:
    if n['pixels'] == 4 and n['color'] not in ['B', 'N']:
        b = n['boundary']
        min_r = min(p[0] for p in b)
        min_c = min(p[1] for p in b)
        frame_blocks.append({'color': n['color'], 'r': min_r, 'c': min_c})

frame_blocks.sort(key=lambda x: (x['r'], x['c']))
rows = {}
for b in frame_blocks:
    r = b['r']
    if r not in rows:
        rows[r] = []
    rows[r].append(b)

print("\nFrame blocks by row after green click:")
for r in sorted(rows.keys()):
    blocks_in_row = sorted(rows[r], key=lambda x: x['c'])
    colors = [b['color'] for b in blocks_in_row]
    print(f"  Row {r}: {colors}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
